source: U.S. Census Bureau, Survey of Income and Program Participation: 2001, 2004 and 2008 panels, wave-2 marital history topical modules (interviews 2001, 2004, 2009), and the 2021 and 2025 annual public-use files; five independent weighted cross-sections, first marriages begun 1960 or later
target: Annual rate of first-marriage dissolution (separation or divorce, dated by the year of separation) per marriage-year from the wedding year; widowhood censored; retrospective histories reported at one interview (Poisson rate, not a probability)
population: U.S. household population aged 15+ who have ever married, men and women, each person’s own FIRST marriage (any spouse)
weights: SIPP final person weights, normalised to mean 1 within each survey, times exposure
timing: Years only (months are suppressed). Weddings and separations are placed mid-year, interviews at their documented point in the year; marriages followed at most 30 years. Inputs are fixed at the wedding.

inputs.marriage_years: completed years since the wedding at the start of the year being scored (0 = wedding year)
inputs.age_at_marriage: age in years in the wedding year (age at interview minus years since the wedding; +/-1 year)
inputs.marriage_year: calendar year of the wedding (1960-2025 in the data); later years are extrapolation
inputs.sex: Woman/Man: the respondent whose first marriage it is
inputs.race_ethnicity: Hispanic, White, Black, Asian, Other (non-Hispanic unless Hispanic; 2001 codes Asian with Pacific Islander)
inputs.education_at_wedding: Only the education model: highest level reached by the end of the wedding year, from the year of the diploma, first college enrolment or bachelor’s degree (2001-2008 modules); Less than high school, High school, Some college, Bachelor or higher, Unknown

abstain: marriages other than the first (a remarriage gets no number from this lens)
age at the wedding outside the support
spouse characteristics are not inputs: the data hold only the current spouse
leakage_note: Spouse traits are excluded: SIPP records the spouse only while the marriage is intact, so using them would encode the outcome. Education at interview is shown only descriptively; it can be completed after the wedding or after a divorce.

models.label: Additive spline Poisson + education at the wedding (2001-2008 panels)

population_reference.method: Weighted percentiles (p1..p99) of HELD-OUT predicted probability of first-marriage dissolution by 5, 10 and 20 years from the wedding, from each person’s own inputs (5-fold household cross-fitting). Subgroups with fewer than 100 people are omitted.
